travel-mode.heading: Travel prep mode.
travel-mode.headingItalic: One click before a trip. Sensei does the rest.
travel-mode.body: Sensei normally holds your charge at the cap you set (80% suggested) so the battery ages slower. The night before a flight, tap Travel prep mode — Sensei lifts the cap, charges to 100%, switches to stricter low-battery warnings (30% / 15% / 5%), and pauses Apple's Optimized Battery Charging. The next morning at 9 AM your normal limit comes back, automatically. No reminder to undo it. No battery left baking at 100% for weeks.
travel-mode.mockupCaption: Limit lifted to 100%. Auto-resets tomorrow at 9 AM.
travel-mode.why: Lithium-ion batteries age faster when held at 100%. A typical "top up before a trip and forget" leaves a MacBook at full charge for weeks — measurably aging the cells. The 9 AM auto-reset is the safety net: even if you forget, the cap returns.

custom-thresholds.heading: Custom thresholds.
custom-thresholds.body: The three included presets cover most days, but if you live by 22% Warning at 14s and 6% Alert until acknowledged, build it. Sensei lets you set the exact percent for each escalation level and how long each card stays on screen. Per-tier, not one global number.
custom-thresholds.mockupCaption: Info · Warning · Alert — each with its own percent and dismiss time.
custom-thresholds.why: One global warning threshold can't serve someone on a long-haul flight and someone in back-to-back meetings the same way. Per-tier thresholds let the nudges fit the day.

alert-presets.heading: Alert presets.
alert-presets.headingItalic: Zen Mode. Regular Mode. Teach Me Senpai.
alert-presets.body: Zen Mode whispers at 15% (closes in 5 s) and once more at 5% (10 s) — quiet, lets you finish. Regular Mode adds a red overlay at 5% and a persistent alert at 2%. Teach Me Senpai keeps it simple but stern: a red overlay at 15% and a full-screen flasher at 5%, both staying until you dismiss. Pick the mood that fits — or compose your own with Custom thresholds.
alert-presets.mockupCaption: Three preset moods. One tap to switch — any time.
alert-presets.why: macOS gives you exactly one battery notification: at 10%. By then it's often too late for the slide you were about to ship. Three presets let the warning match the stakes.

battery-journal.heading: Sensei Saga.
battery-journal.headingItalic: Cycles, charges, rescues — the full history.
battery-journal.body: Saga is the long view of your battery's life. A charge history chart you can flip between 24 h / 3 d / 7 d, a Battery Health panel (capacity, cycles, temperature, condition), the top power-hungry apps over the last hour / day / week, and Spotify-Wrapped-style Weekly + Monthly recaps. When you rescue a battery in time — plug in within 30 minutes of a critical warning — Sensei stitches a Rescue Receipt: a small, shareable card to mark the save.
battery-journal.mockupCaption: Lifetime stats, charge history, Wrapped recaps. All on the Saga page.
battery-journal.why: Battery numbers without context are just numbers. "92% capacity" tells you nothing. Saga gives the same number a story — what it looked like a week ago, which apps cost it the most, which day you nearly lost it.

meeting-battery-guard.heading: Meeting Battery Guard.
meeting-battery-guard.headingItalic: Never miss the meeting that matters.
meeting-battery-guard.body: A Premium feature — included in the free trial, then part of a Lifetime unlock. Opt-in. Sensei reads the next 4 hours of calendar events on-device (EventKit, default lookahead). It scores each meeting against your current battery — Comfortable, Tight, Critical, or Catastrophic — and only nudges when it should. Critical: 30 / 15 / 5 / 0 min before, with the exact minute the laptop would die and the fix ("22 min on the charger and you're clear through"). Catastrophic: warned immediately. Tight: a single 30-min nudge. Comfortable: silent. Plug in early enough and pending warnings cancel themselves. Titles stay readable in notifications by default; one toggle redacts them.
meeting-battery-guard.mockupCaption: 4-hour lookahead. Only nudges when it should.
meeting-battery-guard.why: A 10% warning mid-meeting is useless: you can't leave to find a charger. Reading your calendar lets Sensei warn you when there's still time to fix it — and stay silent the rest of the time.

energy-usage.heading: Top power-hungry apps.
energy-usage.headingItalic: See what's eating your battery, by name.
energy-usage.body: On the Saga page, Sensei ranks the top power users — flip between the last 1 hour, 24 hours, or 7 days. Each app gets an Activity-Monitor-style energy impact score (CPU time blended with idle wake-ups), an impact label (Low / Moderate / High / Very high), and a search filter so you can type "chrome" and watch every Chrome helper line up. Sampled every 5 minutes via per-process resource usage — no system extension, no kernel hooks.
energy-usage.mockupCaption: Top apps · 1h / 24h / 7d · with search filter. Refreshed every 5 min.
energy-usage.why: Battery loss is almost never the battery's fault. It's a hung helper, a sleepless tab, a video call that won't release the GPU. Knowing which app costs you the most is the difference between a 4-hour day and a 7-hour day.

a: Opt-in Premium feature. Sensei reads your calendar locally and predicts which meetings your battery might not survive.

Event titles never leave your Mac. Sensei reads the calendar locally via EventKit. If the risk passes, pending reminders cancel silently.

privacy.title: What we collect.
privacy.intro: Battery Sensei is a small, indie macOS app. We collect the minimum needed to run the site, take payments, and notify you about new versions — and we tell you exactly what that means in plain language below.

controller.heading: Who's responsible for your data
controller.p1: Battery Sensei is operated by <0>Sandro Thabiso Schaier</0>, self-employed individual (živnostník), with business seat at Korunní 2569/108, 101 00 Prague 10, Czech Republic. References to "we" / "us" on this page mean that operator.
controller.p2: Contact for any privacy-related question, request, or complaint: <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0>. We try to reply within a working day.

what.heading: The full list, by surface
what.intro: Battery Sensei the macOS app is privacy-first: it runs entirely on your Mac, with no telemetry, no analytics, no cloud account, and no outbound network calls other than the update check. The list below covers only the marketing website at battery-sensei.app and the order flow on it — which does use cookieless analytics, described in detail below.

items.localeBody: a first-party cookie called <0>bs_locale</0>, written only after you change language via the site switcher. Stores your two-letter locale (e.g. <0>de</0>), expires after one year, never shared.
items.purchaseBody: a session-scope sessionStorage entry called <0>bs_purchase_tracked</0> that prevents duplicate conversion events when you refresh the thank-you page. Cleared the moment you close the tab.
items.analyticsBody: anonymized pageview counters and Core Web Vitals via Vercel Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights. No cookies, no cross-site identifiers; visitor IP addresses are hashed once at the edge before any storage.
items.signupBody: only if you submit the "get the download" form: the email address you typed, the locale of the page, your IP and user-agent (for abuse triage), plus a timestamp.
items.contactBody: only if you write to us via the contact form: name, email, message subject and body, plus IP / user-agent / referring origin for spam protection.
items.checkoutBody: only if you click Buy: the Polar checkout iframe collects your billing details directly. We never touch the card number; we only see what Polar reports back to us (email used, country, receipt id, fulfilment status).
items.logsBody: short-lived request logs at Vercel containing path, status, user-agent and a truncated IP. Used for debugging and abuse triage. Vercel rotates these on a rolling 30-day window.

why.heading: Purpose and legal basis

items.functionalBody: language cookie, purchase-confirmation flag. Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) and Recital 30 of the ePrivacy Directive (strictly functional storage).
items.orderBody: checkout data, license key delivery, refund handling. Legal basis: <0>performance of contract</0> (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
items.newsletterBody: only the email addresses you explicitly submit through the signup form. Legal basis: <0>consent</0> (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), withdrawable at any time via the unsubscribe link in every email, or by writing to <1>info@battery-sensei.app</1>.
items.analyticsBody: a minimum signal of "the site is up and people are reading it". Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in operating and improving the service. No profiling, no advertising re-targeting.
items.abuseBody: IP and user-agent on the contact and signup forms. Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in protecting the service from spam, scraping and fraudulent purchase attempts.

why.noAutomated: We do not engage in any automated decision-making or profiling with legal or similarly significant effects on you (Art. 22 GDPR).

processors.heading: Who actually stores your data
processors.intro: We use a small set of processors. Each has its own privacy policy, linked below. No data we hold is sold or shared with advertising networks.

items.vercelBody: US-based hosting provider, serves the site, runs the server functions, hashes IPs at the edge. Vercel is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Policy: <0>vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.polarBody: merchant of record for all purchases. Handles payment processing, VAT, refunds, license issuance. Card data is collected directly by Polar; we never see it. Transfers to Polar (US) rely on Standard Contractual Clauses. Policy: <0>polar.sh/legal/privacy</0>.
items.resendBody: sends release-alert and transactional emails (purchase receipt, key resend, contact-form confirmation). Email addresses you submit through our forms are mirrored to Resend audiences. Transfers to Resend (US) rely on Standard Contractual Clauses; Resend is also self-certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Policy: <0>resend.com/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.postgresBody: holds the email-signup table, the contact-form table and Polar-issued license records. Provisioned in an EU region (Frankfurt) where the Marketplace provider supports it. Hosted by a Vercel-partner provider; we add their identity here once the production database is wired.

items.signupBody: kept while you stay subscribed. We retain a hashed marker for ~30 days after you unsubscribe to avoid silently re-adding you if you re-submit the form.
items.contactBody: kept up to 24 months from the last reply on the thread, then purged.
items.purchaseBody: Polar, as merchant of record, retains the underlying tax invoice for the legally required period (typically 10 years under Czech Act No. 563/1991 Coll.). We retain only the licence-issuance metadata needed to re-issue or support your key, typically up to 5 years from purchase, after which it is anonymised.
items.logsBody: rotated by Vercel within 30 days of the request.

rights.heading: What you can ask us to do
rights.intro: Under the GDPR (and the Czech Act No. 110/2019 Coll.) you have the right to:

items.access: Request <0>access</0> to the personal data we hold about you (Art. 15 GDPR).
items.correct: Ask us to <0>correct</0> data that is inaccurate or incomplete (Art. 16).
items.delete: Ask us to <0>delete</0> your data when it's no longer needed (Art. 17). For purchase data we have to retain accounting records under Czech tax law.
items.restrict: Ask us to <0>restrict</0> processing while a correction is being assessed (Art. 18).
items.portable: Receive a <0>portable copy</0> of your data in a machine-readable format (Art. 20).
items.object: <0>Object</0> to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21).
items.withdraw: <0>Withdraw consent</0> at any time — the unsubscribe link is at the bottom of every newsletter email.

rights.closing: To exercise any of these rights, email <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0>. We will reply within one month of receipt and may extend this by up to two further months for complex requests, in which case we will notify you within the first month and explain why. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection (Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů, <1>uoou.gov.cz</1>) or with the data protection authority in your country of residence.

merchantOfRecord.heading: Who you actually pay
merchantOfRecord.p1: All purchases on battery-sensei.app are processed by <0>Polar Software, Inc.</0>, our reseller and merchant of record. Polar handles payment, VAT collection and remittance, refunds, invoicing and chargebacks. Your purchase contract for the license is with Polar; your contract for use of the software is with the operator named above. Polar issues the tax invoice in their name — you can re-download it from the link in your purchase email or request a copy from Polar support at any time.
merchantOfRecord.p2: Polar's terms and privacy notice apply to the checkout itself and live at <0>polar.sh/legal</0>.

withdrawal.heading: Your 14-day cooling-off right
withdrawal.p1: As a consumer resident in the European Union, you generally have <0>14 days</0> to withdraw from a distance contract under §1829 of the Czech Civil Code (Act No. 89/2012 Coll.).
withdrawal.p2: Because Battery Sensei is delivered as digital content immediately on payment, by completing checkout you expressly agree that performance begins immediately and acknowledge that, under <0>§1837(l) of the Czech Civil Code</0>, you lose the right of withdrawal once the licence key has been issued.
withdrawal.p3: If your key has not yet been issued, or you have not yet activated it, you can still withdraw within 14 days — write to <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0> and we will coordinate with Polar to refund. Polar's own refund flow (available from your purchase email or the Polar dashboard) is usually the fastest path.
withdrawal.refundCtaHint: Please email from the address you used at checkout — that helps us match your purchase in seconds.

contentLiability.p1: Content on battery-sensei.app is provided in good faith and kept as current as reasonably possible. We do not warrant that every detail is accurate, complete or up to date at any given moment — software, pricing, third-party policies and legal references change.
contentLiability.p2: To the extent permitted by applicable law, we exclude liability for indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages arising out of the use of (or inability to use) the site or the software. This does not limit your statutory consumer rights, which always apply in full.

We have no control over the content of those external pages and assume no responsibility for it. The operators of those pages are solely responsible for their own content.

governingLaw.heading: Which law applies
governingLaw.p1: Use of this site is governed by the laws of the Czech Republic, with the competent courts of the Czech Republic having jurisdiction. If you are a consumer resident in the European Union, the mandatory consumer protection of your country of residence continues to apply in full and is not displaced by this clause.

disputeResolution.heading: If something goes wrong
disputeResolution.p1: We try to resolve any issue directly first — write to <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0> and we'll reply within a working day.
disputeResolution.p2: Consumers in the Czech Republic may also bring out-of-court complaints to the Czech Trade Inspection Authority (Česká obchodní inspekce, <0>coi.cz</0>), which is the designated alternative dispute resolution body under Czech Act No. 634/1992 Coll.
disputeResolution.p3: EU consumers may use the European Commission's Online Dispute Resolution platform at <0>ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr</0>.

privacyPointer.heading: Privacy notice lives separately
